Reopening this, because I found the cause and it is in the library, not my config. Closing it as solved was premature.

PR #812 ("refactor spectral frame handling", merged Oct 22) changed the default in `LineList.__init__` from `wave_frame='air'` to `wave_frame='vacuum'`. Rest wavelengths are now treated as vacuum unless you say otherwise. My data is calibrated in air, so every line is off by the air/vacuum ratio, about 1.00028 at 6563 Å. That is roughly 83 km/s, which matches the shift I see in every object. Downgrading to 2.4.3 restores the old values, which fits this explanation.

m_okonkwo also reports a small offset on long-slit data after updating, so this is not only me.

On "works for me": a fit on vacuum-calibrated or radio data would show no difference, so identical results on your end don't rule this out.

Workaround for anyone with air-calibrated optical data: `LineList(..., wave_frame='air')`.

I'd like two things:
- An explicit line in CHANGES.md saying the default `wave_frame` changed to `'vacuum'` in 2.5.0. "Refactor" does not tell anyone that results can shift.
- A warning (or an error) when `wave_frame` is not set explicitly, at least for one release cycle.

I lost about two days re-checking my arc-lamp wavelength calibration across 40 spectra before finding this. I'd like the next person not to have to do that.
